Nxeon VPS hosting platform, Next.js/TypeScript, repo /opt/nxeon (git, branch `main`).

## Read this framing first — this is NOT a creative-direction task

Three prior attempts at redesigning `app/(marketing)/singapore-vps-hosting/page.tsx` all failed because each one invented its own creative interpretation. The owner has now given an exact visual reference (a ChatGPT-generated mockup) and said explicitly: **recreate this specific design faithfully — keep the purple/navy-blue gradient, but everything else (assets, styling, iconography) should be built to match this reference, not reinterpreted.** Your job is precise implementation of a given comp, the way a frontend engineer implements a Figma handoff — not ideation. Do not invent a different layout, palette, or structure. Where the reference doesn't fully specify something (e.g. an exact icon glyph), make the smallest, most literal choice consistent with the reference's look — don't use it as license to redesign.

## The reference design, section by section (this is the literal spec — build exactly this)

**Global look**: near-black deep-navy background throughout (`--color-navy-950: #060a14` / `--color-navy-900: #0a101f` from `app/globals.css` — use these real tokens, don't invent new hex values). Card surfaces slightly lighter navy (`--color-navy-800`/`--color-navy-850`) with a thin 1px border, subtly violet-tinted at low opacity. The signature accent is a purple-to-blue/cyan gradient (`--color-brand-500: #6f47f5` → `--color-accent-cyan: #22d3ee`, real tokens already in `app/globals.css`, also check the existing reusable `.glow-brand` dual-radial aura class for a real ambient-glow effect already used elsewhere on the site) used consistently on: the gradient headline word, primary CTA buttons, the "MOST POPULAR" badge, the progress-bar fill, "Test now"/link accents.

**1. Hero, two columns.**
- Left: a small dark pill badge with a green status dot + "SINGAPORE DATACENTER" in small caps. Below it, a large headline: "Singapore VPS" in white on one line, "Hosting" on the next line filled with the purple→cyan gradient. Sub-copy paragraph in muted gray about NVMe VPS hosting from a Singapore datacenter, low latency across Asia-Pacific, full root, DDoS, instant deploy. Two buttons: a gradient-filled primary "Deploy now ⚡" and an outlined secondary "See pricing". Below the buttons, a single inline row of small feature bullets separated by dot separators: "Full root access · NVMe + ZFS Storage · Dedicated IPv4 · DDoS Protection".
- Right: a card with a header row "● sgp1  ·  Singapore  ·  [green "Live" badge]", then a spec list (icon + label left, value right, thin divider between rows): vCPU, Memory, Storage, Bandwidth, IPv4, Uptime. Below that in the same card or a connected panel: "Deploying your server" label with "47s" on the right, a horizontal gradient progress bar near 100% fill, "100%" label, "SSH ready" status line. Behind/beside this card: a dark map-style graphic with small glowing dot markers labeled Japan (appears twice, different positions), Vietnam, Indonesia, Australia, and a larger glowing "Singapore" origin dot, connected to each other dot by thin animated arc lines (like flight paths) that pulse/travel outward from Singapore — this is the one element that should get REAL motion (animate the arcs continuously, subtle, respecting `prefers-reduced-motion`).

**2. Feature grid** — 6 bordered cards in a row (wrap on smaller screens), each with a small line-icon on top, bold title, small gray description:
Low latency across APAC / Enterprise NVMe + ZFS / Full root access / DDoS protection / Instant deployment / 24/7 support — use the exact wording style shown (title + one-sentence description each).

**3. Pricing** — heading "Pick your Singapore VPS" + subtext about dedicated IPv4/2.5Gbps+/full management. Four cards side by side (Starter/Standard/Pro/Max): big bold price with small "/mo", a bullet spec list with small check icons (vCPU cores, RAM, NVMe size, bandwidth, dedicated IPv4), a "Deploy now" button (gradient-filled on the most-popular card, outlined on the other three). The most-popular card (Starter) gets a "MOST POPULAR" pill badge (violet) in the top corner and a subtly glowing/highlighted border. A "View all VPS plans →" link below the cards. **Pull the real price from the live plans data source** (check how `UseCaseLanding.tsx`/`page.tsx` currently source plan pricing — a prior audit found the old page's hardcoded copy said $6.49/mo but the DB's real Starter price is $8.88/mo; use the real live number, not a hardcoded one).

**4. Two-column info block**:
- Left: "Network performance across APAC" — a Location/Latency/Test table (Singapore local <1ms, then Malaysia/Indonesia/Thailand/Vietnam/India/Australia/Japan with realistic latency figures), each row with a "Test now →" accent-colored link. Small footnote about latency varying by route. A faint decorative network/particle graphic behind or beside the table.
- Right: "Everything included on every plan" — a 2×4 icon grid: KVM Virtualization, NVMe SSD Storage, Dedicated IPv4, DDoS Protection, Full Root Access, Automatic Backups, IPv6 Support, 99.9% Uptime SLA — icon + title + short description each.

**5. "Deploy in 47 seconds"** — centered heading, a horizontal 3-step flow with numbered circular badges (01/02/03) each next to a small icon box, connected by an arrow/chevron between steps: Choose your plan → Configure → Go live, one-line description under each.

**6. FAQ** — "Questions, answered" heading, a 2-column grid of collapsed accordion rows with a chevron icon (6 questions: location, deployment speed, DDoS inclusion, refunds, upgrade path, available OSes), a "View all FAQs →" link below.

**7. Final CTA banner** — full-width card with a subtle glowing border. Left: a 3D-style isometric graphic of stacked server units with a small glowing Nxeon logo mark. Middle: bold text "Your Singapore VPS is 47 seconds away." with 3 small checkmark lines (no credit card to configure / free migration / cancel anytime). Right: two buttons, "Deploy now ⚡" (gradient) and "View pricing" (outlined).

Header/footer are global site chrome (`MarketingHeader.tsx`/`MarketingFooter.tsx`) — untouched, out of scope.

## What "real motion graphics" means here

The reference is a static image. Bring it to life with real, tasteful motion for the elements that are naturally animated in a real product: the map's arc lines traveling/pulsing outward from Singapore continuously, the deploy progress bar filling with a subtle shimmer on load, gentle hover states on pricing/feature cards, a scroll-reveal for each section as it enters viewport, maybe a subtle count-up on the spec numbers. Keep it restrained and premium, not busy. Respect `prefers-reduced-motion`. Do not change the depicted layout/structure/asset choices to "make room" for motion — the motion serves the given design, it doesn't replace it.

## Technical constraints (same as prior attempts)

- `cd /opt/nxeon && git worktree add /opt/nxeon-wt-sgvps4 -b feature/singapore-redesign-v4`, symlink `node_modules`/`.env`, work only there.
- Do not modify `components/marketing/UseCaseLanding.tsx` or affect the other ~12 pages using it — build this page as its own bespoke component tree. Verify with `grep -rl "UseCaseLanding" "app/(marketing)"` before finishing.
- Real data only for pricing/specs/uptime — no fabricated testimonials or review counts.
- `npm run build` and `npx tsc --noEmit` must pass clean.
- Do not merge to main, do not touch staging/production. Commit on `feature/singapore-redesign-v4` and stop.

## Verification — be thorough here, this has failed 3 times on the visual check

Use Playwright (or whatever's in devDependencies) to screenshot the finished page at 1440px wide (full page, scrolled through so all reveals fire) and 390px wide (mobile). Before reporting done, look at your own screenshot and compare it section-by-section against this spec — if something doesn't match (wrong section order, missing element, wrong color), fix it and re-screenshot. Save the final screenshots somewhere referenceable.

Report back: screenshot paths, commit hash, and a short confirmation that each of the 7 sections above is present and matches the spec (not a creative summary — a literal checklist).
